source_refs.note: Exercise 14.3, Question 8: a x (b + c) + b x (c + a) + c x (a + b) = 0 by distributive and anti-commutative laws (book p.283). Proof, no key answer.

blocks.explanation:
A proof with the algebra of cross products.
We must show the long left side is the zero vector.
Plan: expand by the distributive law, rewrite reversed products with a minus sign, then cancel in pairs.
steps:
Given: any vectors \(\underline{a}, \underline{b}, \underline{c}\).
To prove: the left side equals \(\underline{0}\).
Method: Distributive law \(\underline{u} \times (\underline{v} + \underline{w}) = \underline{u} \times \underline{v} + \underline{u} \times \underline{w}\) (Question 7 (iv)) and \(\underline{v} \times \underline{u} = -\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) (Question 7 (ii)).

Expand each bracket
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \underline{a} \times \underline{b} + \underline{a} \times \underline{c}\]
\[+\ \underline{b} \times \underline{c} + \underline{b} \times \underline{a}\]
\[+\ \underline{c} \times \underline{a} + \underline{c} \times \underline{b}\]
Why: Distributive law, keeping the order inside every product.

Write reversed products with a minus sign
\[\underline{b} \times \underline{a} = -\underline{a} \times \underline{b}\]
\[\underline{a} \times \underline{c} = -\underline{c} \times \underline{a}\]
\[\underline{c} \times \underline{b} = -\underline{b} \times \underline{c}\]
Why: Anti-commutative property: swapping the order changes the sign.

Group and cancel
\[\text{L.H.S.} = (\underline{a} \times \underline{b} - \underline{a} \times \underline{b})\]
\[+ (\underline{b} \times \underline{c} - \underline{b} \times \underline{c})\]
\[+ (\underline{c} \times \underline{a} - \underline{c} \times \underline{a})\]
\[= \underline{0} = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: Each product appears once with \(+\) and once with \(-\); every pair cancels.
